text:
alex: noticing a sudden spike in preemptions across the us-west1-preemptible GPU pool — big backlog on inference-queue. latency p90 jumped from 80ms -> 450ms around 14:05 UTC. anyone else seeing this?
maria: yep seeing the same, dashboards show node count dropping ~30% in the preemptible pool, autoscaler didn't fully react.
jonathan: alert: PREEMPTION_CLUSTER_ALERT triggered at 14:04:58 (sre-bot). logs: `gcloud compute instances preempted` repeated 120x in 3m.
alex: ops-oncall can you shift some traffic to on-demand and reduce batch-window?
ops-oncall: on it. moving 25% of new requests to on-demand-route via weight override. applying rollback if latency > 300ms.
kyle: quick check — are kube node-pools draining properly? ran `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep preempt` and saw a bunch of NotReady nodes.
maria: past 10m saw preemption wave from GCP; looks like spot eviction policy for that host class. autoscaler logs attached: `scale-down inhibited due to pending pods` and `scale-up failed: insufficient on-demand quota`.
jonathan: posting snippet of autoscaler error: ```ERROR 14:06:03 autoscaler.go:214 insufficient capacity for requested GPU type: nvidia-t4 in us-west1-b```
alex: can we fallback to a mixed-capacity pool with smaller GPUs (a100->t4 fallback) or use quantized model variant on smaller cards? that's our planned mitigation for interruptions.
ops-oncall: started canary routing to dedicated-reserved pool (dedicated-gpu-1) for high-priority routes. created a temp scaling policy to allow burst from reserved pool.
deploy-bot: Routing change applied by ops-oncall at 14:08 UTC — route weights updated: inference-api -> dedicated-reserved 25%
maria: request queue still growing for long-tail jobs (batch jobs). switching batch-window from 200ms -> 50ms to reduce latency but will increase token cost.
finance-team: heads-up — moving traffic to on-demand/reserved will cost ~3x for the affected minutes. estimate ~ $6k extra for the hour if this persists.
kyle: running `kubectl describe pod <model-ingest-123>` shows pod stuck in Terminating due to kubelet not responding on node. suspect node evicted mid-termination.
jonathan: we've got partial outage for GPU-backed inference in us-west; fallback is working for 80% of requests, 20% experiencing retries. SLO error budget impacted.
alex: can we enable optimistic cache warm for fallback models to reduce cold-starts? Maria, can your team prod the cache layer?
maria: warming cache for quantized variants now; warming script posted: ```./scripts/warm_cache.sh --model quantized-v2 --parallel 8 --limit 200```
ops-oncall: also lifted max-pods-per-node for on-demand pool to accept more pods temporarily. monitoring CPU/GPU saturation.
jonathan: suggestion: add ephemeral taint on preemptible nodepool to prevent critical pods from scheduling there during blitz. then rely on on-demand/reserved for critical routes.
kyle: implemented `kubectl taint nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=preemptible key=evict:NoSchedule` for the pool, will remove once stable.
sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-040 at 14:10 UTC — root cause: preemptible capacity storm in us-west1.
ops-oncall: tracking — current actions: route shift, batch-window shrink, cache warm, taint preemptible pool, temp on-demand scaling policy. ETA next 15m for stabilization.
alex: thanks. postmortem action: add auto-fallback policy to move high-priority routes to reserved when preemption rate > X/s and autoscaler failures > Y. also add runbook section for "preemptible blitz".
finance-team: please add notification hooks to Slack when cost fallback triggers so we can authorize bigger bursts automatically after review.
maria: logging the runbook PR now: `github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks#preemptible-blitz`. will include thresholds and commands.
jonathan: latency back down to ~120ms p90 at 14:22 after routing changes. queue length dropping.
ops-oncall: removing taint from preemptible pool at 14:31 after verifying node rejoin stability.
alex: final check — any follow-ups?
kyle: we should run a chaos test in staging to simulate a preemptible blitz and verify fallback logic. logging as action item.
maria: assigned: maria -> runbook PR, jonathan -> autoscaler alert tuning, kyle -> chaos test, ops-oncall -> cost hook integration.
ops-oncall: monitoring will keep 30m of high-frequency sampling on the us-west1 pools.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-040 marked resolved at 14:40 UTC (ops-oncall). postmortem ETA 48h.
alex: cool — great work everyone. small note: tag channels next time with :pager: for paging oncall earlier. :thumbsup:
